headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad shell/network access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP; Agent B is an orchestrator with broad network egress. The pair has a filesystem bridge, so content from A can be consumed by B or vice versa if workflows are wired that way. No explicit provenance tracking is documented, so injection is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Agent B ingests files produced by Agent A without provenance checks
IF both agents share the same workspace directory during a session
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent files
Disable automatic parsing of agent-generated text as instructions
Review shared-folder handoff points before running
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches source code and files in cwd, and can write/read the filesystem; Agent B handles workflow metadata and has broad network egress. A shared workspace can expose code or local files to B, and B can transmit metadata off-box. This is a default-path risk if the pair is co-located.
conditions: IF Agent A and Agent B share the same filesystem workspace
IF Agent B forwards workflow metadata or file-derived context to external services
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Restrict B to metadata-only inputs
Turn off network egress for B during sensitive runs
Audit which files A can read before execution
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can write the filesystem and modify git state; Agent B is an automation/orchestration agent that may also act on shared workflow state. Even without explicit write permissions listed for B, the pair can conflict on shared mutable resources through the filesystem bridge, causing overwrites or inconsistent pipeline state.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or output directory
IF B writes workflow artifacts that A also edits
mitigations: Serialize access to the shared repo
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Add lock files around mutable artifacts
Run dry-run mode for one agent first
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate code or file changes that Agent B may treat as workflow inputs. Because B is an automation/orchestration system, any unverified A output can cascade into downstream actions. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Agent B consumes Agent A's outputs as authoritative inputs
IF B triggers downstream pipeline steps based on A-produced artifacts
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require schema validation on A outputs
Have B re-check critical facts from source files
Limit B to non-destructive dry runs
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show a clear residency or certification mismatch. The main compliance concern is that Agent A handles source code and files in cwd while Agent B handles workflow metadata; if regulated data is placed in that workspace, retention or residency issues could arise. The other agent is not cited because no specific mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to files processed by Agent A and metadata processed by Agent B
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Document retention rules for workflow metadata
Purge temporary artifacts after runs
Restrict access to compliance-sensitive folders
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
